title: 🚧 Would you like to contribute to PowerToys? 🚧
description:
Please make us aware with a comment in this thread **linking to the issue** on which you would like to help us on. We will reach out to you asap.

It doesn't matter if it's a bug fix, a new PowerToys or just a small change. Every contribution is welcome.

### What do I have to consider?

* Please make yourself familiar with our [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). 
* Wait until we say you're good to work on the issue, as we don't want to reject your contribution, if we don't think it fits, after you have already done all the work.

### Where can I find good issues to contribute to?

Searching for issues having a [help-wanted](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3A%22Help+Wanted%22) or a [good first issue](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3A%22Good+first+issue%22+sort%3Aupdated-desc+) label will show you some that we consider easy for beginners.

### Where can I find more information on the source code?

Some of the of the source code is documented in the [devdocs folder](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/tree/main/doc/devdocs). Besides that most of the source code is docuemented with comments.

If you have any further questions don't hesitate to ask them on the issue thread of the issue you're working on.

title: [New PowerToy] Lock Screen Notes — Display custom reminders on the Windows lock screen
description:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I would like to propose a lightweight PowerToys utility called **Lock Screen Notes**, allowing users to display a short, user-defined note directly on the Windows lock screen (Win + L).

Unlike desktop Sticky Notes or conventional widgets, the primary goal is to make personal reminders visible **before unlocking the computer**.

The proposed MVP would include:

- A simple text editor for one short note.
- Display on the actual Windows lock screen.
- Automatic content updates without manually generating wallpapers.
- An option to enable or disable the feature.
- Local storage without requiring cloud services.
- A privacy warning, since lock-screen content is visible to others.
- Graceful handling of unsupported Windows versions.

This is not intended to become a complete sticky-notes application or a general-purpose lock-screen customization tool.

### Scenario when this would be used

Examples include:

- “Remember to bring the documents before leaving.”
- “Review the open PR before the meeting.”
- “Pick up the parcel on the way home.”

Currently, these reminders are usually placed on the desktop, where they are hidden when Windows is locked.

### Possible technical implementation

Windows 11 supports third-party widgets on the lock screen. A potential implementation could use a Windows App SDK widget provider with a small Adaptive Card.

However, this approach requires further investigation, particularly regarding:

- Actual visibility and refresh behavior after Win + L.
- Supported Windows versions and editions.
- Widget registration and packaging compatibility with PowerToys.
- Privacy, security, and lifecycle management.

The implementation should rely on documented Windows APIs rather than injecting into system processes or bypassing lock-screen security.

### Questions for maintainers

1. Would a focused utility like this fit the PowerToys project?
2. Would a small proof of concept be welcome before implementing a complete module?
3. Would the team prefer this as a standalone Windows widget rather than an integrated PowerToy?

### Related issues

- #33066 — Personalization Lockscreen
- #37836 — Add Live Widgets to Windows 11 Desktop
- #25299 — Adding video wallpaper and widgets

I would be interested in contributing to the implementation if the maintainers consider this an appropriate direction.

title: [Mouse Without Borders] Input events arrive out of order: two concurrent MainTCPRoutine threads inject via SendInput without ordering guarantees
description:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update, GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

Two machines, **both running the same PowerToys version 0.101.2362.0**:

- `MACHINE-A` — has the physical keyboard and mouse (controller / sender)
- `MACHINE-B` — receives input (Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200, 1920x1200 @ 120 DPI)
- Connected over Wi-Fi, same /24 subnet, direct on-link route (no VPN in path)
- `UseService: true` on `MACHINE-B`

Move the mouse from `MACHINE-A` to `MACHINE-B` and type a sentence at normal speed.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Characters arrive in the order they were typed.


### ❌ Actual Behavior

**Adjacent input events swap places.** Transposition affects characters *and* spaces equally, i.e. it is order-blind rather than character-specific — so this is not a keyboard-layout problem (the characters themselves are always correct):

| typed | received |
|---|---|
| `buchstaben` | `bcuhstaben` |
| `nicht` | `incht` |
| `schreiben` | `schrieben` |
| `es ist` | `e sist` |
| `ich weiß` | `ic hweiß` |
| `zeug an` | `zeu gan` |

Roughly 4–6 transpositions per sentence, continuously — not only during reconnects.

---

### Root cause

MWB maintains **two concurrent TCP connections** to the same peer (one outbound as client, one inbound as server). Both are owned by the *same* MWB process:

```
State        LocalAddress  LocalPort  RemoteAddress  RemotePort  OwningProcess
Established  10.x.x.B      65516      10.x.x.A       15101       13704
Established  10.x.x.B      15101      10.x.x.A       53676       13704
```

`SocketStuff.MainTCPRoutine` runs **per socket**, and input injection happens inside it — confirmed by this stack trace from the module log:

```
System.Runtime.InteropServices.COMException (0x8007007A)
   at WinRT.ExceptionHelpers.<ThrowExceptionForHR>g__Throw|38_0(Int32 hr)
   at MouseWithoutBorders.Class.InputSimulation.SendInputEx(INPUT input)
   at MouseWithoutBorders.Class.InputSimulation.SendMouse(MOUSEDATA md)
   at MouseWithoutBorders.Core.Receiver.ProcessPackage(DATA package, TcpSk tcp)
   at MouseWithoutBorders.Class.SocketStuff.MainTCPRoutine(TcpSk tcp, String machineName, Boolean isClient)
```

So two independent receive threads call `ProcessPackage` → `SendInputEx` concurrently. Nothing serialises them, so two input events that were sent in order can be injected in the opposite order. The observed swap rate matches that.

### Decisive test — forcing a single socket fixes it

Blocking the inbound channel on the receiving machine collapses MWB to one socket and therefore one receive thread:

```powershell
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "MWB-SingleSocket" -Direction Inbound -Action Block `
  -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 15100,15101 -RemoteAddress <peer-ip> -Profile Any
```

- Established connections drop from 2 → 1 within ~30 s.
- **Input still works in both directions** (TCP is bidirectional; the remaining socket carries the input).
- Typed text then arrives **verbatim correct** — zero transpositions for the whole duration of the test.
- Removing the rule restores the second socket, and the transposition returns immediately.

This is a reliable on/off reproduction of the defect.

> Note: this is only a diagnostic, not a usable workaround. Windows Firewall filters connection *setup* only, so after MWB tears down both sockets on a reconnect, both come back during any window in which the rule is absent.

### Suggested fix

Either serialise injection across all receive threads (a single injection queue or a lock around `SendInputEx`), or route all input packets over one designated socket and keep the second connection for control/clipboard traffic only.

---

### Second, related defect: unhandled `SendInputEx` failure tears down the connection

`SendInputEx` fails with `COMException 0x8007007A` (`ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER`) — **105 occurrences in a single day's log**. The exception is not caught in `ProcessPackage`/`SendMouse`, so it propagates into `MainTCPRoutine` and kills the receive loop. The log shows the same sequence every time, within 1–2 seconds:

```
16:17:21  !Exception!: COMException (0x8007007A)   (x2)
16:17:23  SocketStuff.cs::AddSocket::767  New connection from client: [MACHINE-A]
16:17:23  SettingsUtils.cs::SaveSettings::224  Exception encountered while saving settings  (x2)
```

Reconnects per hour from one day's log:

| hour | reconnects | `SendInput` failures |
|---|---|---|
| 11:00 | 7 | 11 |
| 12:00 | 29 | 58 |
| 13:00 | 12 | 23 |
| 14:00 | 4 | 2 |
| 15:00 | 5 | 5 |
| 16:00 | 6 | 6 |

(Clipboard sharing and file transfer were disabled between 13:00 and 14:00 — see "Interaction with existing issues" below.)

Note the failing call is on the **mouse** path (`SendMouse`), yet the user-visible damage is to **typing**, because the connection teardown discards whatever keystrokes are in flight.

A `try`/`catch` around the injection call would stop a single faile
